title: The First Figure of the Year

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: A clean slate is not a clean account. One figure read twice is one figure; the grain under the wool has no voice to answer it.
epigraph.attribution: A saying of the Cross, told on the first market of Ilmen

pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a body of four hundred and two to four hundred and four days, six months and two hundred and twenty-two to two hundred and twenty-four days, carried everywhere in a basket and told by nobody. The old life rides the surgeon's register alone: no present-tense break is spent in this chapter and no \memory{} tag is used, the white room, the page over the speakers and the hands that stayed in the field going on gathering interest from Chapter 113. No departure from the boy's eyes: the Debt Loft is a sound from above and behind, the back room a shape and a dust with men unnamed going low into it before first grey, and the reading at the Cross is a figure passing twice over a basket from the basket's low angle, with Sella standing half a pace off and no Court room entered. Berr Clay is a man come up short off the clay road with the red wool cord folded under his coat and the sweetish green of tasted lead glaze at one mouth-corner, not a confession or a point of view; Hessa Rale goes up the road before noon with the writing turned to her sleeve and is not made a reader by the carrying; Ilva's notched strip stays in her sleeve; the soft-cuffed clerk stays a reported shape set below the north bridge for a measure nobody called; the man from Slate Row is not on stage and his face stays a face on its own tray, never a tenth hand, a sale or a witness. Each morning the register takes the body in its old order — one stiff leathery brown-edged barley crust two inches from the ear with its corner a hair off the wool; the empty place beside it holding the fold of wool Sella put there on the fifteenth, found where put and still a finding, not a placing; the thread of drool frozen in the dry kiln heat and unwiped, because nobody under any roof has ever been given an instruction about the thread; cold stopping at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint where the wool rides back, as at the end of a line written out for it; the Afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform — while the infant's want of the crust lifted, the thread wiped and a hand on the pot handle quarrels without verdict, both true, the second louder, neither winning. Two ordinary tending days and then the new year's first Account-day and market, each day opened by its own dated \daymark and lived in two full scenes; Ilmen 10 is earned by its own morning and is a reset, not a signing, not a thirteenth arithmetic, not a payer and not a doctrine.
places: the flat stone by the well
the reading block under the moot-post

scenes.title: The Eighth Morning
scenes.synopsis: First entry, the chapter's only \dropcap and its first \daymark{402}{Ilmen 8, Y.H. 814, Eighthday}: the small hours opening on the hand laid flat against the fold on answer 378 and the count exact at 401, then first light and the morning under the Vail kiln-house roof. Present: Corin/Dan, Sella Vail, Tarn at the kindling, Jorra Vail at the wheel-shed edge; Garl Vail in objects only (salt-stiff coat with its left-shoulder crease on the peg, hollow wheel-seat, clean dark line at the Vail corner with its finer grey called the thaw thickened in the dry cold with the faint sour tang of Ash, twice-mended pot's hairline between old-brass staple and tighter wire, unforged collector sentence at the kindling, uncalled tile debt). Walk-ons only: neighbours going about an ordinary Eighthday in the Clay Yard. No Berr, Hessa, Ilva, collector, officer, market, Cross or bell; no ownerless voice over the boards — the Ash 5 joining and the Ash 17, Ash 23 and Stone 23 directions stand where put, do not repeat and buy no lesson (T035/T031/T065/T095 held). New day, new date, no recap: the hand on the fold is the present moment, not a retelling, and nothing from the working week crosses forward as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer; Ilmen 10 stands two mornings off and is not brought. Dramatic purpose: the surgeon takes the body in its old order and knows a face composed by cold is not composure, that a cold patient cannot clot and must be rewarmed slowly from the outside, never hurried, never rubbed, and that pink returning is the surface still lying over a cold core, while the infant's three wants quarrel without verdict, both true, the second louder, neither winning (T060/T086). The boy keeps four hundred and two exact against a house that keeps its days in loaves, glances and an unnamed space at the row's end and does not stand the number up as a threshold or a figure (T071/T072). Sella comes to the hearth before the basket, tells the coals it is the thaw and turns them with the back of a broken pot, gives intake, hold and letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, keeps her finger above the unread charcoal, moves her lips on a two-gapped row, glances once at the clay jar cold under lead glaze with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air, lifts the twice-mended pot thumb-first where the wire crosses the crack with the hairline showing and both proverbs to pot and fire, turns the dressed grain under wool with no figure or handful and sets the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed; she carries him down and up the nineteen steps at the half-pace from every open slate, goes wide around the seven walked-around places once and not twice, widest around the returning-line place, sets him under the roof and never in the Debt Loft, adds no second fold, and leaves the widow's mark untouched (T058/T079/T100, T077, T009/T013/T092, T098 carried). At the kindling Tarn keeps six where the house can check and the seventh at the lip beside Garl's unforged sentence, passes his hand over blade and sill and away with no breath held at the top of the reach, tells the wood *Six counted. The next I don't count*, and does not turn his head toward the landing; the ear-sentence stops at the calling word as a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth, the Seed 16 breath stays unspent, the loan uncalled and the fear of vagrancy his without a figure (T036/T076/T006). At the wheel-shed Jorra parts dusty forearms from clean as clot from vessel, speaks to the wheel before any person, knows a pot's full note three turns ahead and withholds it, and puts his bent finger into the cold damper ahead of Sella's unfinished sentence without the extra holding of Ash 26 a second time; *he's not Vail* stays sealed and the promise under the shed neither given nor withdrawn (T062/T035/T031). Answer 379 filed: exact, complete, worth nothing at two inches of air, a restraint and not a payment borrowing no house count and supplying no payer; six honest answers stand on the sixth place, 374 through 379, not one a doctrine. The carried fire gives four low pulls with the fifth unsupplied, its payer unnamed four hundred and two days; Garl's name unspoken the same number, the two counts standing side by side without becoming one (T088). Textures: elm-bark smoke, tallow, grey dust ground small as meal past a bent finger, the leathery crust gone harder in the dry heat, cold stopping at wrist, the river's note low under its winter skin through the finger's-width door. Foreshadowing planted, not paid: the first arithmetic of the year waits two mornings off as a reset and not a signing, and the boy does not lay his twelve old findings across a figure that has not yet been read (T015/T041/T047 held). Emotional turn: the adult's exact inventory of a body at rest held against the infant's loud hunger, neither winning, the surgeon finding a small clean satisfaction in a field taken as found and left as found and knowing it costs nothing. Last image: the hand outside the wool comes up an inch toward the river's note under its winter skin (the inch is not a reach), takes a small intake from the room whose floor does not touch his, holds the interval whole on the note's own finishing, lets it go as the note ended — neither early nor stayed — and comes straight down and lays itself flat against the fold on answer 379, the crust's corner standing a hair off the wool and the thread frozen and unwiped.

scenes.title: What the Eighth Day Left
scenes.synopsis: Second entry, no new dated heading: Ilmen 8 afternoon through the going of the light and the small hours closing the day, with answer 380 and the count standing at 402 exact. Present: Corin/Dan, Sella Vail, Tarn at the kindling and flagstones, Jorra Vail at the wheel-shed edge and the cold damper; Garl Vail in objects. Walk-ons only: neighbours going about the yard, a woman setting a pail down where she always sets it, a loaf pushed a finger's width along a board and stopped with nobody calling the stopping a figure, two voices passing the price of barley from one end of the wall to the other without making a number of it, a neighbour with a rake looking at the ridge at the Vail corner and looking away. No Berr, Hessa, Ilva, called collector, officer, market, Cross or bell; no slate opened within reach of the basket and no figure given for the boy; no ownerless voice over the boards. New day already dated in Scene 1; nothing crosses forward from the morning as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer. Dramatic purpose: the yard goes on in its ordinary grammar and the boy takes the small sounds first because they do not lie and the large ones are mostly weather; he goes around the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number, once and not twice, widest around the returning-line place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come back, and gives the wide step no name, cause or figure, for a figure would want a payer standing and none stood (T098, T009/T013/T092). He keeps the called-gone grey the yard will one day burn beside the left-in-place ridge at the Vail corner with a finger between, and makes no fourth likeness a cause (T083/T085). Sella comes to the hearth before the basket at the going of the light, tells the coals it is the thaw, turns them with the back of a broken pot, keeps her finger on top of the loaf shelf so the charcoal tally stays unread, lifts the twice-mended pot thumb-first with the hairline showing, says both proverbs to pot and fire and never to a person, turns the dressed grain under wool with no figure or handful, sets the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, and carries him up the nineteen steps and under the roof and never into the Debt Loft, adding no second fold (T077, T058/T079/T100, T097 held). Tarn takes the broom only after it has been given its instruction, says *Yes, house* to the thing behind the asking, keeps six in the worn thumb-mark and the seventh at the lip, passes his hand over blade and sill and away with no breath held at the top of the reach, tells the wood *Six counted. The next I don't count*, and does not repeat the degree toward the landing; the warm loft stone stays unreconciled by not trying, which is not forgiving (T036/T076/T006). Jorra knows the full note of a Vail pot three turns before it leaves his hands and withholds the knowing from any High Kiln master who would call it early; he speaks to the wheel and a pot before any person and keeps the shed's silence (T062/T035/T031). In the small hours the towel comes out at the head of the bed as instruments come out when a case is done, and the boy goes over the field by the place of each thing with every gap left a gap: the crust's gap, the shelf's two gaps, the gone pan's round ring, the field's empty place, the keeping at the fold found where put and still a finding, the told bell's gap in its square beside the heard bell, the silence after the name from Weighing on the gap tray beside the clean voice's missing name and the Long Night story's empty name, the called-gone grey beside the left-in-place ridge, Tarn's ear-sentence stopped at the calling word in a term already ended, Jorra's promise neither given nor withdrawn, the clerk's inward slate at the out-of-line landing, Tarn's degree held as a shape and not repeated, and the man from Slate Row's face on its tray, filed and not counted among the nine record-first hands, never a tenth, never a sale, never a witness (T080/T090, T078, T061/T082, T081). Answer 380 filed; six honest answers on the sixth place, 375 through 380, not one a doctrine. Sensory anchors: pail set on stone, barley passed mouth to mouth, rake lifted and set aside, wet wool and banked coals, the towel rough from the wash and smelling of tallow and low smoke, the fourth low pull under the floor and the silence where the fifth stood. Foreshadowing: Ilmen 10 remains one morning beyond the close and is named nowhere as a threshold; the kindness Berr will say over the block is not anticipated. Emotional turn: the house's arithmetic kept badly in loaves and glances against the boy's exact count, and the satisfaction in a field left as found, which is not peace. Last image: the hand comes straight down on answer 380 and lies flat against the fold with the crust's corner standing a hair off the wool, the thread frozen and unwiped, four low pulls breathing below the floor with the fifth unsupplied, and the next morning still unbrought.

scenes.title: The Ninth Morning
scenes.synopsis: Third entry and the second dated \daymark{403}{Ilmen 9, Y.H. 814, Ninthday}: the small hours opening the day, then first light and the morning's work, with answer 381 and the count at 403 exact. Present: Corin/Dan, Sella Vail, Tarn, Jorra Vail; Garl Vail in objects. Walk-ons only: neighbours at the well and along the yard; a glaze-hand come down the clay road with the sweetish green at one corner of his mouth is not on stage in this scene. No Berr, Hessa, Ilva, collector, officer, market, Cross or bell; no slate opened within reach of the basket and no figure given for the boy; Ilmen 10 stands one morning off and is not brought into a day that has not earned it. New day, new date, no recap: nothing from Ilmen 8 crosses forward as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer. Dramatic purpose: the surgeon takes the body in its old order and reads the crust gone harder through the dry nights, the fold found where put, the frozen thread, cold stopping at the small bare wrist-joint and the Afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform, while the infant wants the crust lifted, the thread wiped and a hand on the pot handle — both true, the second louder, neither winning (T060/T086, T097/T060/T086). Sella comes to the hearth before the basket, tells the coals it is the thaw in the voice another woman would use for a child who could not hear her, turns them with the back of a broken pot, counts intake, hold and letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, keeps her finger above the charcoal, lifts the twice-mended pot thumb-first with the hairline of the original break showing between old-brass staple and tighter wire, says both proverbs to pot and fire and never to a person — *Leave the crack showing. People trust a thing they can see has been handled* and *If it's worth mending it's worth mending twice. The second time is the real one* — keeping repair apart from restoration as a surgeon keeps a graft apart from a cure, turns the dressed grain under wool with a touch lighter than a woman would use on a sleeping child and no figure or handful, and sets the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed (T009/T013/T092, T077). She carries him down and up at the half-pace from every open slate, goes wide around the seven walked-around places once and not twice, sets him under the roof and never in the Debt Loft, and adds no second fold; the widow's mark is not touched, because a morning, a hearth, a shelf and a basket are not openings and seven openings in seven months are seven and not a rule (T058/T079). On the boards a wrong wind off High Kiln brings the sweet edge of lead glaze over the yard and out again on the wind that brought it, a direction arrived nowhere with no hand at the kiln and no name under it; the boy files it on a place of its own beside Berr's green and the market greens and makes no lesson or cause of it (T064). Tarn at the kindling keeps six where the house can check and the seventh at the lip, tells the wood *Six counted. The next I don't count*, lets his hand go over blade and sill and away with no breath held at the top of the reach, and does not turn his head toward the landing; the ear-sentence stops at the calling word, a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth, the Seed 16 breath unspent and the loan uncalled at the end of a term already ended (T036/T076/T006). Jorra comes through the finger's-width door from the room off the wheel-shed with the day's meal-fine grey slate dust white in a fist-crease, not the bone-coloured slip; he parts dusty forearms from clean as clot from vessel, asks neither which slate was broken nor whether it was a birth-slate, and withholds the full note he knows three turns ahead (T035/T031/T062). Answer 381 filed; the carried fire gives four low pulls with the fifth unpaid four hundred and three days and Garl's name unspoken the same number (T088). Sensory anchors: woodsmoke in wet wool, the sour tang of Ash at the unswept corner, the twice-mended pot's hairline dark between two metals, a wrong wind carrying the sweet edge of glaze, the bare wrist-joint where the wool rides back. Foreshadowing: the arithmetic that will be read on the morrow is not laid across the twelve old findings and does not stand up as a signature; the reset is not spoken of as a door. Emotional turn: the adult's knowledge of how a thing holds a break and the child's hunger for the crust set two inches away, with Sella's proverbs going to the pot and the fire and never to a person. Last image: the hand outside the wool comes up an inch toward the river's note under its winter skin, holds the interval whole on the note's own finishing, lets it go as the note ended, and comes down and lies flat against the fold on answer 381 — the keeping at the fold found where put, no second fold, the fifth pull under the floor unsupplied and the morrow still unbrought.

scenes.title: The Last Quiet Day
scenes.synopsis: Fourth entry, no new dated heading: Ilmen 9 afternoon through the going of the light and the small hours closing the day, with answer 382 and the count at 403 exact. Present: Corin/Dan, Sella Vail, Tarn, Jorra Vail; Garl Vail in objects. Walk-ons only: neighbours in the Clay Yard, a man counting kindling into a stack and not counting the stack, a woman setting a pail down where she always sets it, a voice passing the price of barley from one end of the wall to the other without making a number of it, a neighbour with a rake looking at the ridge and looking away and nothing said. No Berr, Hessa, Ilva, called collector, officer, market, Cross or bell; the man from Slate Row is not on stage and his face stays on its own tray, neither called nor paid; no slate opened within reach of the basket, no figure given for the boy, no ownerless voice over the boards. New day already dated in Scene 3; nothing crosses forward from the morning as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer, and the coming reading is not made a boundary, a door or a rule. Dramatic purpose: the yard goes on in its ordinary grammar on the last quiet day, and the boy takes the field as found and leaves it as found, going around the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number, once and not twice, and keeping the wide step as a keeping and not a sign (T098, T009/T013/T092). A number rises out of a fist toward the yard, looks at the light and goes back into a sleeve, and a woman sent to the pot gets no figure from a pot; costs arrive as directions and go away as weather and leave no entry (T077). The boy does not stand tomorrow's arithmetic up as a threshold: one reading will be one and not an account, a reset is not a signing, and twelve old findings must not be laid across a new figure to make a row come out even, for a row made even by a hand that has no key is a row made even on paper and paper is not a payer (T015/T041/T047 held). Sella at the going of the light tells the coals it is the thaw, keeps her finger along the top of the loaf shelf so the charcoal stays unread, lifts the pot thumb-first with the hairline showing and both proverbs to pot and fire, turns the dressed grain under wool with no figure or handful, sets the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, and carries him up and under the roof and never into the Debt Loft, putting the fold right at his ear and under his chin without a look at his face and adding no second fold (T058/T079/T100, T077, T097). Tarn passes his hand over blade and sill and away with no breath held at the top of the reach and tells the wood *Six counted. The next I don't count*, cutting, counting and spending nothing; his degree toward the landing is a shape found where put and not made a second time, a habit or a rule (T036/T076/T006). Jorra's bent finger goes into the cold damper ahead of Sella's unfinished sentence and comes out without the extra holding of Ash 26 a second time, one piece of iron with the holding and the taking and no Grathic word for both mercies; the promise under the shed stays neither given nor withdrawn and the burned-slate word stays at five (T062/T035/T031/T065/T095). In the small hours the nine record-first hands stand with no tenth, the clerk's reported hand on its own tray and the clean-voice speaker taken out of his own sentences, and the face at the edge filed beside them and not counted among them (T080/T090). Six hearings of the full note stand beside and never among with the seventh place empty and the Drawing's flat knock outside it; the burned slate at five, the shut-room tellings at two, the row at five askings with one shaping and no witness, the well-saying at four shapings and the four old directions stand where put and do not repeat and buy no lesson (T061/T082, T101). Answer 382 filed; six honest answers on the sixth place, 377 through 382, not one a doctrine. Sensory anchors: kindling stacked and not counted, pail on stone, barley passed mouth to mouth, rake lifted and set down, the wool folded once in the empty place, the four low pulls under the floor and the silence of the fifth. Foreshadowing planted: the first arithmetic of the year stands one morning off, a reset and not a signing, and the boy keeps his twelve old findings on their own place rather than even a row; the kindness not yet spoken over the reading block is not anticipated. Emotional turn: a field taken as found and left as found gives the surgeon a satisfaction that costs nothing, which is how he knows it is not peace, while the infant's three wants go on quarrelling under it without verdict. Last image: the hand comes down on answer 382 and lies flat against the fold, the crust's corner standing a hair off the wool and the thread frozen and unwiped, and Ilmen 10 waits one morning off without a boundary drawn around it.

scenes.title: One in Twelve, as the Notice Says
scenes.synopsis: Fifth entry and the third dated \daymark{404}{Ilmen 10, Y.H. 814, Tenthday}: before first light, then the first Account-day and market of the new year at the Cross, with answer 383 and the count at 404 exact. Present: Corin/Dan, Sella Vail, Berr Clay, Hessa Rale; Garl Vail in objects. Offstage but kept on their own places: Tarn, Jorra Vail, the soft-cuffed clerk at the out-of-line landing, the man from Slate Row. Walk-ons only: the two hundred at the Cross, a man with a number in a shut fist, a silent woman across the square at the pot board with green at one mouth-corner, a shape at the market's edge, neighbours passing the bell from mouth to mouth. No collector called, no Court room entered, no interior for any walk-on, no name spoken over the green or the shape, no loaf, slate or sale passing between them, and the adult romance stays planted years ahead and unspent. New day, new date, no recap: the reading belongs to Ilmen 10 and does not cross back over Ilmen 8 or 9 as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer; a tend-day is not set against a holy day. THE CHAPTER'S ONE MEANINGFUL CHANGE, advanced and NOT paid: the new year's first arithmetic is read over the basket and the district's arithmetic begins again and cannot be undone. Berr Clay comes up short off the clay road with the red wool cord of his office folded square under his coat and the sweetish green of tasted lead glaze at one mouth-corner, under the hot clay of him the smell of nothing at all; he wipes his thumb twice before touching nothing, holds a narrow slate unopened to his forearm, passes a finger over the figure through his sleeve, reads *One in twelve, as the notice says* low into the goers-by, sends it twice over the basket — once for the moot and once for the households that come late — calls the levy and denies it with *your house*, never *I*, taking himself out of his own sentence as a surgeon draws a hand from a field before the dressing goes on. He says something low to the reading block about kindness being entered, with no anger and no triumph in him and no payer standing, and sends a man with a number in his fist to a slate at the watch; the number goes from fist to mouth to shoulder and arrives nowhere. He goes off up the clay road toward High Kiln with the box locked and the new year's first true subtraction inside, believing he has done a kindness (T015/T041/T047 advanced, not paid). This is the first arithmetic of Y.H. 814 and NOT a thirteenth: one reading is one and not an account, the reset supplies no payer, no signature stands on the space and no doctrine comes out of one; the boy does not lay his twelve old findings across the new figure to make a row come out even, and the figure read aloud is still not the figure paid (T015/T041/T047, T061/T082). Sella sets the basket in the moot-post's finger's width of shade where no slate lies and stands half a pace off through the reading and the bell, carrying him home at the going of the light saying nothing of what was read over the wicker (T058/T079). Hessa goes up the clay road before noon toward Greybank with the narrow slate edge-on to her forearm and the writing turned to her own sleeve, her hand to the slate before her eyes to the crowd, giving no figure and not made a reader by the carrying; her eighth hand stays eight and joined to none (T080). The soft-cuffed clerk stays set below the north bridge at the out-of-line landing with his slate turned inward for a measure nobody called, reported and not witnessed, and Tarn's degree toward it from Ilmen 3 stays a shape not repeated (T090/T036/T076). The bell goes four, four and a gap with nobody crossing himself, the heard bell kept in its square beside the told bell and its gap not folded into the fire's four and a gap under the floor, the boards' four and four and a thumb-width knot, or the three counts in three places (T078, T061/T082). A green at the pot board and a shape at the market's edge stay sightings with no eighth of either, never Fenna or Ulda in the narration, no second look joined and no name given (T050/T051, T033/T034 held). The boy files Berr's low saying about kindness being entered on a place of its own, with a finger between it and the twelve old findings and between it and the new figure, and joins neither; the kindness is not paid and is left to gather against the day it is remembered against him (T015/T041/T047, T080). Sensory anchors: the moot-post's finger's width of thin shade and the cold iron of the basket at his cheek, red wool folded under a coat, green at a mouth-corner, a thumb wiped twice on an apron, the slate held inward, the bell going longer than a church bell, the clay road going up toward High Kiln with the box in a locked cart, pigs going over the weighing board unfigured. Foreshadowing planted: Berr's kindness on the first reading of the year, the figure that does not know the dressed grain's cost, the clerk's uncalled measure and the green and the shape all go on gathering toward far-off accountings, none paid here. Emotional turn: the district's arithmetic changes for the year and cannot be changed back while the figure read over the boy is still not the figure paid and nobody addresses the boy it will carry; his satisfaction is exactness in a field taken as found, not mercy and not peace. Last image: the figure has gone twice over the basket and the number for the thaw has gone from a shut fist to a shoulder and arrived nowhere, the bell keeps four, four and a gap beside the told bell, and Berr's box goes up the clay road with the first true subtraction of the year inside while Sella stands half a pace off with the basket in the moot-post's shade.

scenes.title: The Arithmetic Gone Up the Road
scenes.synopsis: Sixth and final entry, chapter close, no new dated heading: Ilmen 10 afternoon through the going of the light and the small hours closing the chapter, with answer 384 and the count at 404 exact. Present: Corin/Dan, Sella Vail; Garl Vail in objects. Offstage with keepings found where put: Tarn at the kindling and flagstones, Jorra Vail at the wheel-shed and cold damper, Berr Clay up the clay road with the box locked, Hessa Rale gone up the road before noon with the writing to her sleeve, Ilva at the well with her strip in her sleeve, the soft-cuffed clerk at the out-of-line landing, the man from Slate Row on his tray. Walk-ons only: neighbours settling into the ordinary grammar of the tend. No second reading brought forward, no market after the going of the light, no collector called, no present-tense break and no \memory{} tag. New day already dated in Scene 5; nothing from the reading crosses back under the roof as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer, and Ilmen 20 (Day 414), the month's second Account-day, stands ten mornings beyond the close and is not brought. Dramatic purpose: Sella goes to the hearth before the basket at the going of the light, tells the coals it is the thaw, turns them with the back of a broken pot, gives intake, hold and letting-go toward no opening with neither gap figured, keeps her finger on top of the loaf shelf so the charcoal stays unread, lifts the twice-mended pot thumb-first where the wire crosses the crack with the hairline showing and both proverbs to pot and fire, turns the dressed grain under wool with a touch lighter than a woman would use on a sleeping child and no figure or handful — the figure read that morning over the grain covered at home did not know what it cost, and the space between the two figures has no signature — and sets the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed (T077, T058/T079/T100). She carries him up the nineteen steps at the half-pace from every open slate, goes wide around the seven walked-around places once and not twice, sets him under the roof and never in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right at his ear and under his chin without a look at his face and adds no second fold; the keeping at the fold is found where put and stays a finding, still not a placing, with no second fold, third crust, name, gift, payment or payer (T097/T060/T086). The widow's mark is not touched — an Account-day, a market, a shelf, a bed and a going of the light are not openings, seven openings in seven months are seven and not a rule and no eighth is made due (T058/T079). In the small hours the towel comes out at the head of the bed as instruments come out when a case is done and before the next is called, and the boy goes over the field by the place of each thing with every gap left a gap: the crust's gap, the shelf's two gaps, the gone pan's round ring, the field's empty place, the keeping at the fold found where put and still a finding, the told bell's gap in its square beside the heard bell, the silence after the name from Weighing and the clean voice's missing name and the Long Night story's empty name on the gap tray, the neighbour's called-gone grey beside the left-in-place ridge at the Vail corner, Tarn's ear-sentence stopped at the calling word in a term already ended, Jorra's promise under the wheel-shed neither given nor withdrawn, Garl's unforged collector sentence beside the seventh notch and his name unspoken the same number as the fire's fifth, the clerk's inward slate and Tarn's degree on separate places, Berr's low saying about kindness entered on a place of its own beside neither the twelve findings nor the new figure, and the man from Slate Row's face on its tray, filed and not counted among the nine record-first hands (T080/T090, T078, T061/T082, T081, T009/T013/T092, T036/T076/T006). Six hearings of the full note stand beside and never among with the seventh place empty and the Drawing's knock outside; nine hands stay nine with no tenth and nine stoppings nine with no tenth, and no eighth opening, seventh hearing, thirteenth arithmetic, signature, payer, witness, reader or payment stood (T061/T082). The first arithmetic of Y.H. 814 stands gone up the road in Berr's locked box with the key gone up in a coat pocket that never comes back down and the boy having no key; it is one reading and not an account, and he does not lay twelve old findings across it to make a row come out even, for paper is not a payer (T015/T041/T047 held, not paid). Answer 384 filed: exact, complete, worth nothing at two inches of air, a restraint and not a payment borrowing no house count and supplying no payer, laid across neither the twelve readings, the new figure, the bell's gap, the flat knock, the child's grey fingertips, the mother's cup, the covered grain, the handful, the thumb's resting, the held breath, the two bites of iron, the river's skin, the widow's mark, the fourth direction, the clerk's inward slate, the face at the edge nor the keeping at the fold; six honest answers stand on the sixth place, 379 through 384, and not one is a doctrine. Count four hundred and four exact, six months and two hundred and twenty-four days told by nobody; the carried fire's fifth unpaid and Garl's name unspoken the same number, the two counts standing side by side without becoming one (T071/T072, T088). The surgeon takes his small clean satisfaction in a field taken as found and left as found and knows that it costs nothing, which is how he knows it is not peace; under it, louder, the body wants the crust lifted two inches, the thread at the mouth wiped and a hand on the pot board's handle, and gets none of the three. Nothing was opened, joined, named, called, paid, forgiven or ended, and no door was drawn across the tend. Sensory anchors: tallow and low smoke in the rough towel, the crust's corner a hair off the wool, the thread stiff and unwiped, cold at cheek, temple and bare wrist-joint, the river's note low under its winter skin through the finger's-width door, four low pulls under the floor with the fifth unsupplied, four nails on the near board, four on the next and a thumb-width knot where a fifth might have been driven and was not. Foreshadowing: the first reading gone up the road gathers interest toward the district's far-off accounting; Berr's kindness, the collector's reason, the clean voice's missing name, the Long Night story's empty name, the clerk's inward slate and the face at the edge go on their own trays toward the hand not his that will lay the private keepings together; the second reading of Ilmen stands ten mornings off and is not brought early. Emotional turn: the year's first arithmetic has changed the district and left the house exactly as it found it, and the boy keeps the exactness without making a doctrine of one reading. Last image: the hand outside the wool comes up an inch toward the river's note under its winter skin, takes a small intake from the room whose floor does not touch his, holds the interval whole on the note's own finishing, lets it go as the note ended — neither early nor stayed — and comes straight down and lays itself flat against the fold on answer 384 as a man puts away a tool where the next hand will find it without looking; the crust's corner stands a hair off the wool, the thread is frozen and unwiped, four low pulls breathe below the floor with the fifth unsupplied, the first arithmetic of the year is up the road in a locked box with no key in his hand, and the house goes on as a house goes when a pot is set down in its place and the fire kept — forward.
